t: The Secretary shall conduct a study to determine the feasibility of carrying out a project for ecosystem restoration, flood damage reduction, and recreation at Lake Merritt, Oakland, California.

fable.w: The section only directs the Secretary to conduct a feasibility study for a project at Lake Merritt. The tempting reading is that a local project in Oakland implies coordination with local government or the public, but the text requires no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: The Secretary shall conduct a study to determine the feasibility of carrying out a project for ecosystem restoration, flood damage reduction, and recreation at Lake Merritt, Oakland, California.

qwen_block.w: This section mandates the Secretary to conduct an internal study regarding the feasibility of a project. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from any parties outside the federal government (such as the public, state/local governments, or experts) before making a decision. The mere act of studying a project's feasibility is an internal government function.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary shall conduct a study to determine the feasibility of carrying out a project for ecosystem restoration, flood damage reduction, and recreation at Lake Merritt, Oakland, California.

opus.w: The section only tells the Secretary to conduct a feasibility study. It names no outside party and sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue. It is tempting to assume that a local project means working with the City of Oakland or other non-federal sponsors, but the text says nothing of the kind, and a study alone is not participation in a federal decision.
opus.s: The Secretary shall conduct a study to determine the feasibility of carrying out a project for ecosystem restoration, flood damage reduction, and recreation at Lake Merritt, Oakland, California.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through:** A tempting reading is that a feasibility study for a project in a specific city (Oakland) implies working with local governments or non-federal sponsors. But the text names no outside party at all. It only tells the Secretary to conduct a study, and a study is not itself a decision that outsiders take part in (see Example 3). Nothing here crosses the federal boundary.

qwen_chat.w: The section mandates the Secretary to conduct a study, but it does not require consultation, coordination, or input from any parties outside the federal government. Conducting a study is an internal executive action unless the statute explicitly requires public comment, advisory committees with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes. qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall conduct a study to determine the feasibility of carrying out a project for ecosystem restoration, flood damage reduction, and recreation at Lake Merritt, Oakland, California.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that a "study" implies gathering input from outside experts or the public, thus constituting participation.
